code_learning: state identity + desired primary-dominant 0.6/0.4 mixture decoding; no operator/transition semantics
interpretation: A six-dimensional codebook learned only to preserve primary identity under 0.6/0.4 mixtures can replace the explicit 32-way common-action probability vector at the fusion layer in this controlled screen. The learned code decodes all 1024 one-hot state pairs correctly and matches the explicit probability-mixture discrete outcomes across all three source pools/depth1-10.
claim_boundary: The codebook is learned from externally known state identity and the desired fusion dominance law, not from transition semantics. Source adapters still form common-action probabilities before projecting to the latent expectation. This demonstrates learned fusion-safe compression, not a label-free latent transition space.
